text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Catalan President Jordi Pujol defends pact with Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar because it gives greater "dividends" than agreement with previous Socialist government.
- First meeting between Aznar and Cuban President Fidel Castro concludes in failure.
- Government says plane which flew via Madrid's Barajas airport to Rwanda in 1994 was carrying food, not arms.
- Attorney Ignacio Gordillo under investigation for links with lawyer of Herri Batasuna (Popular Unity), political arm of Basque separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
EL MUNDO

- Unidentified men hit, torture and rape last "protected witness" against General Enrique Rodriguez Galindo, suspect in kidnapping, torture and murder of two presumed Basque guerrillas during a 1980s "dirty war" on ETA.
- Aznar tells Castro: "I have nothing against Cuba, but I do against your regime."
- Internal document proves U.S. contemplating return to Torrejon military base.
DIARIO 16
- Democratic Convergence of Catalonia (CDC), member of Catalan Convergence and Union (CiU) coalition, reelects Pujol as leader and demands Catalan football squad.
ABC
- Dictator Castro rejects Aznar's offer of representing him in European Union on condition of democratising Cuba.
CINCO DIAS
- 500,000 customers cancel mobile phones in boom year.
- Savings banks continue to prefer deposits to investment funds.
- Consumption flat, growth flat.
- Bank of Spain fights drug money laundering.
EXPANSION
- Exchequer cancels 30 billion pesetas insurer debt for one-off premiums.
- Telepizza share price set at 2,300 pesetas, will start trading Wednesday.
- Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti seeks buyer for his 48.05 percent stake in Corporacion Financiera (Cofir).
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Iberia wants to head group together with KLM, Swissair and Alitalia.
- Government will promote global alliance between Telefonica and AT&T.
